title: Race and Equality: Giving the Cause

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *debido a* and *a raíz de* from B1 Unit 6: formal ways to give a cause, always followed by a noun (*debido a un error*). A text about racial inequality in Brazil explains causes and results all the time, in a calm, formal tone. Here the connectors work on that topic.

sections.title: Formal causes
rows: Debido a la falta de tierras, muchos libertos tuvieron pocas oportunidades.
*debido a* + noun: because of the lack of land
A raíz de la ley de 2012, las universidades federales reservan plazas.
*a raíz de* + noun: as a result of the law
Hubo debates porque la ley cambió el acceso a la universidad.
*porque* + verb: because the law changed access
Los estudios mostraron desigualdades; por eso se crearon nuevas políticas.

items.spanish: Debido a la abolición de 1888, millones de personas dejaron de ser esclavizadas.
items.english: Because of the abolition of 1888, millions of people stopped being enslaved.

items.spanish: A raíz de los estudios de Florestan Fernandes, cambió la imagen de Brasil.
items.english: As a result of Florestan Fernandes's studies, the image of Brazil changed.

items.spanish: Debido a la ley, más estudiantes negros e indígenas entraron a la universidad.
items.english: Because of the law, more Black and Indigenous students entered university.

sections.content: *Debido a* and *a raíz de* take a noun, never a verb: *debido a la ley*, not *debido a que se aprobó*. With a verb use *porque*. They sound formal, so they suit a report or an article more than a chat.
